author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
The QBID part appears resolved under the standard comparison setup. With `--assume-w2-wages` (the flag we use for all eCPS-style comparisons since TAXSIM has no W-2-wages-from-business input):

- **PE QBID**: $187,837.84
- **TAXSIM QBID**: $187,837.83

So PE does apply QBID when W-2 wages aren't artificially zeroed by the input. PE-US's QBI sources at [`gov/irs/deductions/qbi/income_definition.yaml`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/master/policyengine_us/parameters/gov/irs/deductions/qbi/income_definition.yaml) include `self_employment_income`, `partnership_s_corp_income`, `rental_income`, `farm_rent_income`, `farm_operations_income`, `estate_income`. The `psemp` TAXSIM input maps to `self_employment_income`.

On your broader pass-through taxonomy:

| TAXSIM input | PE-taxsim → PE-US | FICA in PE? | QBID in PE? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `psemp`/`ssemp` | `self_employment_income` | Yes (SE tax) | Yes | Matches your "FICA, no QBID" framing only if QBID is suppressed |
| `pbusinc` | `qualified_business_income` | No | Yes | Matches "QBID, no FICA" |
| `pprofinc`/`sprofinc` | `sstb_self_employment_income` | Yes | Yes (with SSTB phase-out at high income) | Matches "QBID w/ phaseout + FICA" |
| `scorp` | `partnership_s_corp_income` | No | Yes | Currently no SSTB phase-out applied; passive-vs-material participation question (see #930, #943) |
| `otherprop` | `miscellaneous_income` (per PR #931) | No | No | Per § 1411(c)(1)(A): subject to NIIT but not QBID; current mapping skips NIIT |
| `nonprop` | (unmapped?) | No | No | |

Three legal questions on your proposed framing:

1. **psemp + QBID**: Your proposal says "psemp = FICA but not QBID" — but § 199A(c)(3) defines QBI to include net earnings from a qualified trade or business, which generally covers Schedule SE income (other than reasonable compensation paid to S-corp owners). Current PE-US treats `self_employment_income` as QBI-eligible, consistent with the form's default treatment.
2. **scorp passive vs active**: TAXSIM's scorp slot is ambiguous. Per § 1411 + § 469, K-1 income from passive S-corp is NIIT-eligible. Per § 199A(d)(2), SSTB-style services trades have a phase-out. We need an explicit input flag to disambiguate.
3. **otherprop NIIT**: Separately tracking that — current PR #931 mapping bypasses § 1411(c)(1)(A) which the NBER docs explicitly require for `otherprop`.

Happy to align with whatever framework you settle on — would you like a separate audit doc walking each variable through statute + state-tax-instructions impact?

(No TaxAct PDF in this bundle, so I can't anchor the residual $25K federal gap between PE and TAXSIM to a specific statute line.)
